messages:
zara: Quick triage: after the scheduled KMS rotation + yesterday's tighter egress allowlist, a subset of GPU warm-pool nodes in ca-central-1 are stuck in INIT. Keystore decrypt calls either 403 or hang until timeout and autoscaler can't reach target. Sample from node-init logs:
```
2026-06-02T07:41:02Z node-init ERROR keystore decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException KMS:Decrypt (src=10.250.5.18)
2026-06-02T07:41:04Z warmup WARN join attempt=5 -> backoff
2026-06-02T07:41:07Z net DEBUG egress route lookup: privatelink endpoint resolved to 10.250.4.0/24
```
This is in two AZs only. App traffic unaffected but capacity runway shortened.

peter: Noted. The new egress policy only references the static privatelink ENI IPs we had during design; during rotation the privatelink DNS resolved to freshly provisioned ENIs in the keystore-subnet (ephemeral). Our allowlist was IP-based, not DNS/plist-based. Also saw fallback to NAT and conntrack pressure.

olga: audit exporter retried PUTs to S3 after keystore failures -> PUT amplification. We already have P95 keystore-handshake at ~65s on affected nodes. ops-bot alerted earlier.

ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-warmup-join-failure-rate > 6% (10m). keystore-decrypt-p95 = 65.2s.

mike: Proposed quick mitigations (minimal blast radius):
- add a temporary route for keystore privatelink using the endpoint's managed prefix-list (pl-0a1b2c) so we match ephemeral ENIs instead of hard IPs
- add a scoped SG egress rule allowing traffic from keystore-tagged ENIs CIDR (10.250.4.0/22) to port 443, TTL 45m
- enable node-local keystore cache in the runtime for 5m TTL to avoid repeated KMS roundtrips during rotation (low-risk config change)
I can run route + SG changes via CI after approval.

zara: I like route + cache first. The SG change is fallback if route can't be applied in both AZs quickly. We cannot loosen IAM conditions right now. Pre-authorize the route change, deploy cache to staging canary.

peter: CLI snippets: add managed prefix-list route (will scope to subnet route table):
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0e1f2g3h --destination-prefix-list-id pl-0a1b2c --gateway-id vpce-05xx --dry-run
```
And SG egress (temp):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0caffe00 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.250.4.0/22 --description "temp allow keystore ENIs"
```
I'll open infra PR with revert TTL and link this thread.

olga: cost note: if we have to scale warmpool by +2 per AZ for 2h to cover capacity it's ~ $2.6k/region. S3 PUT storm could cost similar amounts long term; flipping sample rate to 20% immediately reduces S3 spend while we fix.

mike: ops-bot, can you flip sampler to 20% and apply route change to staging now?

ops-bot: action: audit-sampler -> 20% (deploy id ds-5512). Attempting route apply in staging.

ops-bot: staging: route apply succeeded in AZ-a, canary keystore decrypt p95 -> 210ms (was 5.2s). Applying to prod AZs in rolling fashion.

zara: Applied route in prod AZs + added node-local cache config to warm-pool launch template (canary baked). Within 18m, affected nodes reporting keystore decrypt p95 ~ 190ms and joins completing. Audit PUTs down ~75% after sampler flip.

peter: Terraform PR opened: infra#2113 - add privatelink-managed-prefixlist route + canary + revert TTL 1h. Also added rotation-runbook update: pre-seed prefix-list and test DNS-to-ENI mapping before rotation.

mike: Followups: 1) update rotation runbook to include "pre-warm keystore cache" step and to verify prefix-list resolution 2) switch allowlist model from static IPs to prefix-lists or service-name where supported 3) add a metric that detects fallback-to-NAT for keystore flows so we catch this earlier.

cost-bot: NOTE: projected incremental cost if mitigation extended >3h = ~$7k. Current window contained; estimated net delta for this incident ~ +$1.5k thanks to sampler and short TTLs.

zara: Closing: prod warm-pool stable 40m after route+cache. Leaving monitoring open for 1h then will mark resolved and add postmortem notes. Thanks team :thumbsup:
